title: Audit shared-object resolution and introduce deterministic soft-fallbacks for CUTLASS/Triton kernels
creator: Ava Patel
description: Problem: The runtime still relies on non-deterministic RTLD symbol resolution paths and a mix of hard-coded plugin probes which cause intermittent kernel mismatches across heterogeneous fleets. This increases cold-start jitter, complicates canary rollouts, and leads to emergent regressions when upgrading CUTLASS/Triton/CUDA stacks. Goal: perform an audit of shared-object resolution and pkg-level probes, remove legacy probe fallbacks that cause symbol shadowing, and implement a deterministic soft-fallback mechanism that prefers validated kernel bundles while allowing graceful degradation to quantized or slower kernels when necessary. Deliverables: audit report, small refactor of the runtime loader, a deterministic selection policy implementation, unit and e2e tests, canary rollout plan, and telemetry to measure pre/post impact on cold-start and kernel mismatch rate.
acceptance_criteria: Audit doc with list of offending shared objects and exact causes of symbol collisions published to Confluence
Runtime introduces deterministic kernel selection policy (manifest-based) gated behind a feature flag
Soft-fallback behavior implemented: when a preferred kernel bundle fails to initialize, runtime falls back to a validated alternative rather than re-probing arbitrary system symbols
End-to-end tests that simulate mixed CUTLASS/Triton versions and assert deterministic selection and successful fallbacks
Canary rollout executed to 5% of Dedicated fleet with observability dashboards showing no >2x regression in P99 cold-start and kernel-failure rate reduced by >=60%
Linked PRs merge and release artifact includes audit checksum and signed kernel-manifest
Backout plan documented and verified in staging
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Created ticket - initial scope and risks documented. Identified three immediate areas: rpath/runspath handling, duplicate symbol providers (libcutlass.so variants), and legacy probe helpers under /opt/runtime/plugins.
2026-03-11: Local audit run on dev-fleet: reproduced symbol shadowing scenario using older Triton plugin; collected ldtrace and objdump snapshots. Attached sample traces to Confluence.

2026-03-12: Spike completed for manifest-based selection. Prototype manifest format drafted (bundle_id, abi_fingerprint, kernel_profiles, fallback_chain). POC runtime hook implemented in branch runtime/feature/deterministic-loader.

2026-03-13: Wrote unit tests that assert selection chooses signed bundle over system library when feature-flag enabled. Initial CI failing due to test environment not mocking ldconfig; fixed by adding wrapper shim in CI image.

2026-03-14: Integration test run on staging: successful fallbacks to int8-quantized kernels under simulated allocation failures. Observed 40% reduction in kernel-init errors during warmup. Preparing canary plan and PR review.
notes: Trade-offs considered: full namespacing of all vendor symbols is safest but high-risk/large change; we chose manifest + feature-flagged deterministic selection to minimize blast radius. Short-term shim to prefer signed bundles introduced; long-term plan is symbol namespace isolation. Rollout: start with non-production canary, then Dedicated low-traffic pools, then general rollout. Telemetry to add: kernel_init_failures by bundle_id, cold_start_ms by image, symbol-shadowing incidents. Backout: disable feature flag and revert loader change; retain audit artifacts to trace incidents. QA: will run hetero-arch stress harness (nvlink-enabled and non-nvlink nodes) and a small perf benchmark measuring GEMM P50/P99 before merging.
